title: The 10 Best Cordless Snow Blowers
subtitle: Battery snow blowers and powered snow shovels for driveways, walks and decks, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: Battery snow removal splits into two kinds of tool. Powered snow shovels (12-16 in wide) clear steps, decks and walks after a light snowfall; walk-behind blowers (16-24 in) handle driveways. We ranked 10 best-sellers from EGO, VOLTASK, WORX, Greenworks, Snow Joe and Vibekio on rating, review volume and features (a battery in the box, a path 16 in or wider, a brushless motor and a throw of 25 ft or more). Check whether the battery is included: two picks are bare tools.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: EGO Power+ 21" Cordless Snow Blower with Steel Auger, (2) 56V 5.0Ah Batteries and Dual Port Charger (SNT2112)
products.verdict: Amazon's top-selling cordless snow blower. A 21" steel auger, variable auger speed and two 5.0Ah batteries in the box make it the closest thing here to a small gas single-stage.
products.best_for: Driveways that get regular 4-8 in snowfalls.
products.skip_if: Your storms drop more than 8 in at a time; that's two-stage territory.
pros: Two batteries, dual-port charger and LED headlights included
cons: Single-stage: rated for 8 in of snow

products.name: EGO Power+ 24" Cordless Self-Propelled 2-Stage XP Snow Blower, (2) 56V 10.0Ah Batteries and Dual Port Charger (SNT2416)

specs.runtime: Up to a 24-car driveway in 8 in (listed)

products.verdict: A self-propelled two-stage machine that runs on batteries. EGO rates it for a 24-car driveway in 8 in of snow on one charge, with heated grips and trigger steering.

products.skip_if: You clear a short driveway; it's 198 lb and $1,799.

avoid.name: Westinghouse WSnow18 48V Cordless Snow Blower 18 Inch Kit, Steel Auger, LED Light, 1200W Brushless Motor
avoid.verdict: It costs more than the VOLTASK 48V 20 in blower and lists half the runtime on a narrower path. The listing also disagrees with itself on throw distance and voltage.
reasons: Listed runtime is 15 minutes in 7 in of snow; the $269.99 VOLTASK 48V lists 30 minutes and cuts a path 2 in wider
Title says it throws 25 ft; the spec table says 20 ft
Spec table lists 120 volts on a battery tool that runs two 24V packs

buyers_guide.a: A cordless snow shovel is a handheld auger 12-16 in wide that you push like a shovel. It suits steps, decks, walks and a short driveway after 6-8 in of snow. A walk-behind blower (16-24 in) rolls on wheels and clears a two-car driveway much faster.

A single-stage blower uses one auger to pick up and throw snow, and it scrapes down to the pavement. The single-stage picks here are rated for 8-10 in. A two-stage machine adds an impeller, so it handles deep, wet and plowed-in snow, but it's heavier and costs far more.

buyers_guide.q: How much runtime do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Listed runtimes on this page range from 15 to 30 minutes on the included batteries; EGO and WORX quote driveway sizes instead. Wet snow drains a battery faster than powder. If your driveway takes longer than one pack, buy into a battery system where a spare is easy to find.

buyers_guide.q: Does the battery come with it?
buyers_guide.a: Not always. The EGO SNS1200 and Greenworks Gen 2 are bare tools for people who already own those batteries. Every other pick on this page includes a battery and charger.

buyers_guide.q: What do clearing width and depth mean?
buyers_guide.a: Width is the path cut in one pass. Depth is the deepest snow the intake handles. Snow deeper than the listed depth has to be taken in two passes, so match depth to your usual storm.
